title: Boys Are Breaking Their Own Faces to Look Like 'Chads'
author: Bradley, Anthony
summary: A new and dangerous male body dysmorphia crisis is emerging among boys and young men driven by social media platforms that promote extreme appearance standards. The trend -- called looksmaxxing -- ranges from skincare and weightlifting (softmaxxing) to jaw treatments, abdominal etching, and even trying to reshape facial bones through blunt force (hardmaxxing). Doctors report rising rates of body-image disorders, eating disorders, and risky supplement and drug use among males as young as 11-13. The idealized male archetype being promoted online -- square jaw, muscular build, almond eyes, flawless skin -- is being pursued through influencer-promoted use of testosterone, anabolic steroids, and isotretinoin, all of which carry serious health risks. Men now constitute 25-30% of cosmetic surgery patients in some practices, with many in their 20s and 30s. The author calls on parents and churches to directly address this crisis with preteens, teens, and young men, arguing that curricula even a few years old have no framework for the specific online environment boys are navigating today.
points: * Appearance-related anxiety, long associated mainly with women, is now affecting males of all ages, with peak vulnerability at ages 11-13 and older teens. * Social media platforms are systematically shaping boys' body image toward an unattainable masculine ideal, creating a form of male body dysmorphia without historical precedent. * Even ostensibly healthy behaviors like high protein intake can become dangerous when taken to extremes under the influence of looksmaxxing culture. * Influencers promote off-label use of testosterone, anabolic steroids, and Accutane, which carry risks ranging from cardiovascular events to liver damage and mood disorders. * Parents and churches that rely on curricula from even a few years ago -- focused on apologetics or quiet times -- are already behind in addressing what boys are actually encountering online.
quotes: We have a national catastrophe on our hands, and installing Covenant Eyes will not protect any son or young man you know.
If you know a boy or young man on Instagram, Snapchat, or similar platforms, those apps are shaping his body image and the cosmetic changes he believes he needs to make to his body.
If you are not having these conversations with your sons, you are missing the window to step in before this becomes something far worse.
This is not a fringe issue. It is everywhere in the lives of young guys right now, and if your playbook is a curriculum from even a few years ago, you are already behind.
